title: Airway Management Flow
sources: Critical Vector — Physiologically Difficult Airway (PREOXI, PREPARE II, RSI trial 2025)

changelog.change: Added a physiologic-optimisation step (four deadly profiles) and NIV/PEEP preoxygenation per PREOXI; cross-linked the new physiologically-difficult-airway reference + modified-shock-index + capnography.
Initial entry — workflow that orchestrates existing Calculators and Drug & Dosing content.

purpose: A workflow wrapper that orchestrates existing calculators and drug cards into a pre-intubation → Plan A/B/C/D → confirmation sequence. Not new clinical content.

nodes.body: Run LEMON (and STOP-BANG / ASA class in an elective or procedural context). Identify a difficult airway BEFORE committing. Prepare a double set-up (surgical airway kit open) if LEMON flags multiple features.

Anatomy predicts the view; physiology decides survival. Screen for the four deadly profiles — hypoxemia (shunt), hypotension (SI > 0.8 / MSI ≥ 1.3), metabolic acidosis (compensating minute ventilation), RV failure — and resuscitate them BEFORE induction. Pressor on the pole, not a reflex fluid bolus. See the Physiologically Difficult Airway reference.

NIV or a tight-fitting BVM with PEEP (not a nonrebreather alone) if SpO2 won't climb toward 95% — PREOXI. 3 min or 8 vital-capacity breaths. Apneic oxygenation via nasal cannula at 15 L/min through induction and laryngoscopy (low-risk; adds little once NIV preoxygenation is adequate).
Direct or video laryngoscopy with your standard induction agent + paralytic (see the Drug & Dosing cards). Optimise position (ear-to-sternal-notch), external laryngeal manipulation, bougie ready.
Change one thing: alternate blade or a video device, add a bougie, reposition, second operator. Limit to a small number of attempts — each attempt worsens oedema and desaturation.

nodes.prompt: 5. Plan C — can't intubate, can oxygenate
nodes.body: Insert a supraglottic airway (LMA) as rescue oxygenation. Reassess: wake the patient if feasible, or proceed to a definitive airway with the most experienced operator.

nodes.prompt: 6. Plan D — can't intubate, CAN'T oxygenate (CICO)
nodes.body: Declare it out loud. Proceed immediately to a surgical airway / scalpel-bougie cricothyrotomy. Do not keep re-attempting laryngoscopy.
Waveform capnography (gold standard) + bilateral breath sounds + no epigastric sounds. CXR for depth. Secure the tube, set the ventilator, start post-intubation sedation/analgesia.
Record the Cormack-Lehane grade obtained, number of attempts, devices used, tube size and depth at the lip, cuff pressure, and any complications.

checklist: Difficult-airway assessment done (LEMON) and backup plan verbalised
Suction, two working laryngoscopes, bougie, SGA, and a surgical airway kit at the bedside
Induction + paralytic drawn up and dosed (see Drug & Dosing)
Capnography connected before the first attempt
buildNote: Depends on LEMON, STOP-BANG, ASA, Cormack-Lehane (Calculators) and the RSI drug cards (Drug & Dosing). Cormack-Lehane is not yet a built module — cross-link will resolve once it is.
